claim: The redesigned regular GC round targets O(delta) plus O(servers) S3 requests; its only universe-proportional operation is the existing LIST sweep, which costs O(universe/1000) LIST requests.
The ack-floor redesign replaces the per-round all-shard fence R3, the fold-through-fence recheck R4, and the separate per-server watermark object.

Before the redesign, 100,000 tables with 8 root shards each required approximately 800,000 CAS-PUTs and 1,600,000 GETs per GC round because the fence and recheck traversed the entire root-shard universe.
Each server maintains one merged heartbeat object at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`, replacing the separate `roots/<server-hex>/_watermark` object and `WatermarkKeeper`.

The merged heartbeat body carries the existing mount fields plus `min_active_build_seq`, `observed_gc_round`, and `gc_fenced`; `observed_gc_round` is monotone and `gc_fenced` is terminal for the incarnation.

The separate `process_epoch` field is dropped because the writable path already sets `process_epoch = writer_epoch`; the merged heartbeat's `writer_epoch` serves both mount and orphan-sweep epoch roles.
The proposed unified heartbeat cadence is 3–5 seconds, satisfying the watermark freshness requirement, the `mount_lease_ttl_ms` = 30 s TTL/3 rule, and GC acknowledgement latency bounds.

The current retired-candidate set is stored as per-GC-shard artifacts using the strict `cas_retired_set` protobuf codec (`RetiredSetProto`, magic `CART`), with entries sorted by `(kind, hash)` and each entry containing `(blob_hash, token, condemn_round)`.

The retired list is one current sorted candidate set referenced by `gc/state.retired_refs`; per-round retired sets keyed by `retiredKey(...)` and the multi-round `RetireView` fetch protocol are removed.

The retired-list and `condemn_round` protobuf fields are additive fields in the same compatibility regime as `snap_attempt`; no per-object version integer is bumped, and future `compatibility_version` values fail closed.

`gc/state` removes `fence_version`, adds current retired-list references and checksums, and is updated with one CAS per pass containing the round, generation adoption, retired references, and coverage.
A GC pass must durably write retired-list and snapshot runs before the `gc/state` CAS that publishes `round := K`, so any reader observing round K can load retired-list version K.
`fence_round` is no longer bumped every round; it remains only as the birth floor stamped at root-shard creation for THM-NO-RETURN newborn ordering.

A mounted writer acknowledges a GC round only after it has loaded that round's retired list, drained all old-view `mutateShard` calls, and installed the new view; the advertised `observed_gc_round` never exceeds the installed and drained view.
If `gc/state` is unavailable during a writer heartbeat, the writer does not advance its GC acknowledgement but still renews its lease; this can stall deletion globally without taking writers down.
Writable open ordering is claim heartbeat, load `gc/state` and the retired list, stamp `observed_gc_round`, and only then enable mutations.

At the commit gate, a blob incarnation whose `(hash, current_token)` appears in the retired list must be recreated from build-local source with a token-conditional overwrite; the retired token is never referenced.

Condemned-blob recreation uses the existing `Build::putBlob` cold-reuse rule on a retried build; the promote gate remains fail-closed with `ABORTED` because build-local sources are not retained at promote time.
GC computes `min_ack` as the minimum `observed_gc_round` among live heartbeats; terminated heartbeats are excluded, and if no live heartbeats exist then `min_ack = +∞`.

An expired heartbeat without a terminated stamp is fenced out with a token-guarded overwrite that sets `gc_fenced` and bumps `seq`; successful fence-out makes the sleeper's next renewal fail and excludes it from the acknowledgement floor.
GC fence-outs complete before discovery and their writers' last commits are therefore durable before the sweep begins.

Discovery performs one paginated LIST of `cas/refs/` and ETag-diffs it against per-shard folded tokens; backends with `supportsListTokens = false` use per-shard HEAD/GET and remain fail-closed and read-only.

The GC merge processes the prior snapshot run, sorted edge deltas, and prior retired run with three cursors sorted by `blob_hash`, emitting the new snapshot run, retired run, and delete list in one streaming pass.
A retired candidate with recovered in-degree greater than zero is spared and removed from the retired output; the implementation emits a B170 recheck-verdict event with the recovered in-degree.
A retired candidate with zero in-degree graduates only when `condemn_round < min_ack`; a zero-in-degree candidate with `condemn_round >= min_ack` remains in the retired list.
A zero-in-degree candidate not already retired is condemned by HEADing its blob, capturing its current token, and appending `(hash, token, K)` to the retired output; an absent blob is skipped.
The inequality `min_ack ≤ K−1` prevents an entry condemned in pass K from graduating in that same pass, so the two-round condemnation pipeline follows from the round arithmetic.
Graduation is two-phase: a pass marks fresh graduates with `delete_pending = true` and keeps them published, while `deleteExact` runs only for entries already pending in the previous published list.

A pending delete is terminal: a pending entry with recovered in-degree is spared and logged loudly, while re-executing a pending delete is safe at any leader staleness; a failed CAS cannot publish a zombie leader's fresh decisions.

`deleteExact(hash, token)` treats `Deleted`, `TokenMismatch`, and `NotFound` as completed delete outcomes; a token mismatch means a writer recreated a fresh live incarnation, which can be re-condemned by a later round.
The GC crash-resume regime uses attempt-scoped write-once artifacts; an already-executed delete is replayed through the `NotFound` branch, and only the adopted attempt is reader-visible.

The redesigned steady-state round budget is one LIST sweep plus O(servers) heartbeat GETs, O(D) changed-shard GETs, O(window) manifest GETs, O(gc_shards) run GET/PUTs, candidate HEADs, graduated DELETEs, O(D) coverage PUTs, and one `gc/state` CAS, with no O(universe) GET/PUT phase.

For the 100,000-table by 8-root-shard slowly-changing example, the redesign estimates 2,000–3,000 requests costing approximately $0.001–0.01 and seconds per round, versus approximately 2,400,000 requests and $4.6 today.

A delete at pass K is safe because a writer with view `V ≥ condemn_round` sees the retired token and recreates it, while a writer with `V < condemn_round` must have been terminated or fenced out before the sweep and its commits are folded into the same merge.
The heartbeat drain proves that a server advertising `observed_gc_round = A` has no in-flight commit using a view below A.

A mount created during a GC pass either participates in the enumerated heartbeat floor or, if pagination misses it, loads a view at least as new as the last published round before its creation and therefore sees every entry eligible for graduation.

The local write-fence deadline should use a `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`-based clock because `steady_clock` (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`) does not advance across VM suspend; container pause remains safe because the monotonic clock keeps ticking.

A fence-out is terminal for an incarnation but a live server can self-remount by creating a fresh incarnation; `Store::tryRemountOnce` repeats the durable epoch bump, `claimMountAwaitingExpiry`, retired-view load, and write-fence arming, while older-epoch builds fail closed with `ABORTED`.
The first 1-hour soak found that a 51-second pause concurrent with a GC round could brick a writer until manual restart; the self-remount rule addresses this S13 liveness failure.

GC observability includes heartbeat acknowledgement lag, B170 condemn/spare/graduate/delete/fence-out events, retired-list size and oldest-entry age, and an invariant alert for changed shards whose pre-fold events are not folded.

The ack-floor migration is pre-release and does not support persisted-data compatibility or mixed-version pools; it removes watermark objects, `fence_version`, per-round retired sets, and fence/recheck paths, starts with an empty retired list, and carries folded tokens and cursors through existing seals.
Snapshot-run streaming scope includes T2 streaming reads and T0 reference-parent runs for empty-delta shards; T1 delta-runs are deferred to a subsequent specification.

Before T2, a snapshot run was materialized three times—by `CasObjectStorageBackend::get`, `RunFileReader::full`, and `readPriorEdges`—for peak memory of approximately 3 × O(active edges) per GC shard; the target example estimated about 24 GB RAM for one fold.

Before T0, every pass rewrote every GC-shard snapshot run even for an empty delta, causing an idle pool to pay two snapshot sizes per round; at the target scale and 5-minute rounds this was estimated as terabytes per day of churn.
`Backend::get(key, Range)` must perform a true ranged object-storage read using `seek` and a bounded read window, not read the whole object and apply `substr` afterward.

`Backend::getStream(const String & key, Range range = {})` returns `{std::unique_ptr<ReadBuffer>, Token}` as a forward-only read of a write-once object; mutable objects such as shards, `gc/state`, and mounts must continue using `get`.
Opening a snapshot run in streaming mode uses a HEAD, a ranged tail GET for the footer, and a body `getStream`; resident run memory is O(block) while the wire bytes are unchanged.

`RunFileReader` has borrowed-memory and streaming modes; streaming mode retains only the footer index and one current block no larger than `kRunHardCapBlockSize` = 1 MiB, while `seek` uses a ranged GET for the target block.
Streaming run reads verify per-block and footer CRCs and treat a short or truncated stream as `CORRUPTED_DATA`, never adopting a partial parse.
The design rejects one ranged GET per block for full scans because an 8 GB run would require approximately 32,000 requests per shard per pass; ranged block GETs remain only for `seek`.
When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the new `fold_seal` carries the parent generation's `RunRef` key and checksum verbatim and performs no run GET or PUT for that shard.
`RunRef` has an explicit additive `shard` field so consumers associate a run with a GC shard without parsing key paths; run consumers resolve through seal references rather than constructing keys.

Retention must preserve any run object referenced by the live adopted seal; when a later pass replaces a parent reference, it deletes the superseded old-generation prefix after the CAS, with a crash window that can strand at most one small object per shard in the original design.
With T0, an idle round that has no changes touches zero snapshot-run objects and consists of the LIST sweep, heartbeats, and one `gc/state` CAS.

The landed streaming implementation makes a large-footer run a fourth request instead of three: a tail probe that does not cover the footer triggers one exact-footer ranged GET, while the resident-memory bound is unchanged.

Implemented retention skips at generation granularity and advances `snap_pruned_through` over every visited generation; when a reference moves off a skipped generation, hand-off deletes the whole `gc/gen/<g>/` prefix rather than one run, preventing leaks of the rest of that generation's artifacts.

S13 occurs when a hard-killed server leaves a same-UUID mount body with the old `writer_epoch` and a future `expires_at_ms`; startup has already bumped the epoch, so the one-shot `claimMount` reports `LiveDoubleStart` and aborts before lease expiry.

`claimMountAwaitingExpiry` retries the unchanged `claimMount` only for a same-UUID `LiveDoubleStart`; it immediately returns `ForeignOwner`, returns `Claimed` after token-guarded reclamation, and returns `LiveDoubleStart` after the bounded wait expires.

The mount-reclaim wait deadline is latched from the first stale lease's `expires_at_ms` plus a margin and capped at no more than one TTL plus margin from the wait start; no new user setting is introduced.

Production mount-reclaim polling is derived as approximately `mount_renew_period / 2`, with the margin approximately one poll interval; the wait uses the existing `mount_lease_ttl_ms` and `mount_renew_period` settings.
Mount reclamation is safe because `claimMount` overwrites the observed mount token conditionally; a live holder that renews between observation and reclaim changes the token and cannot be stolen.

`claimMountAwaitingExpiry` accepts injectable wall-clock and sleep functions so unit tests can advance a fake clock without real sleeping; production uses a system-clock reader and `std::this_thread::sleep_for`.

`Store::open` calls `claimMountAwaitingExpiry` after bumping `writer_epoch`; it logs the first wait and throws the existing `ABORTED` double-start error only for a foreign owner or a lease that remains live through the wait bound.
The mount crash-recovery change does not modify `claimMount`, the owner anchor, the epoch counter, or the watermark, and it adds no user-facing configuration.
A different-UUID stale mount remains a fail-closed `CORRUPTED_DATA` foreign-owner condition and requires operator guidance rather than automatic takeover.

The D1 1-hour chaos soak ended with `table_rows` 1,765,870, `fsck reachable=0, unreachable=0, dangling=0, dryrun_count=0`, zero aborted-retried inserts, zero transport-retried operations, and no failed GC finish rows.
During the D1 soak, memory remained flat with approximately 1.6–2.0 GB per ClickHouse replica and no OOM; disk usage returned to 507 GB free after teardown.

The D1 soak observed physical pool usage peaking at approximately 39.7 GiB while logical bytes were approximately 101 MiB, attributed for follow-up to full-GC/B140 debris and possible RustFS overwrite-version retention rather than a safety defect.

The D1 report identifies fsck scalability as follow-up work: `clickhouse-disks fsck` timed out after more than 180 seconds on a pool with approximately 1.7 million rows, although the final converge fsck completed cleanly.
The D2 scenario sweep had 14 PASS, 10 INCONCLUSIVE, and 8 FAIL results, and reported zero D1 regressions; D1-specific scenarios S30, S34, and S35 passed.

D2 found that the S23 idle-pool `s3_ops` metric incorrectly summed `*Microseconds` ProfileEvents as operation counts; the measured CAS counts were `CasRootList=0 CasRootGet=0 CasGcGet=71 CasGcPut=24 CasGcList=9` and `S3ReadRequestsCount=17`.
D2 classified S19 and S26 replica-agreement failures as harness synchronization races because the checks did not run `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` before comparing replicas.

D2 classified S13's failure to become healthy within 240 seconds after killing ch1 as a harness/chaos issue downstream of the connection refusal, not a D1 regression; the recommended fix is to re-run and inspect the kill/restart mechanism and health timeout.

Without a valid `gc/state` baseline, trimmed journals make a fresh GC interpret long-committed live blobs as zero-in-degree and mass-delete live data; this is fail-catastrophic rather than fail-closed.
A fold using an empty baseline must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` when a discovered ref shard proves trimmed history: `journal.front().transition_version > 1`, or an empty journal with `shard_version > 0`.
The baseline guard gates GC only; it never blocks server startup or normal reads and writes, and a genuinely fresh pool whose journals start at version 1 passes.

If `snap_generation > 0` but the adopted fold seal, a referenced run, or a referenced retired object is absent or corrupt, GC must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` rather than treating the artifact as an empty baseline.
`Gc::rebuildBaseline` writes only the GC plane—runs, seals, and `gc/state`—and never modifies ref shards, manifests, or blobs or deletes content.

The rebuild is live-conservative: events after a shard read remain above the recorded cursor for the next regular round, a live precommit with an absent body clamps the cursor below its transition, and new condemnations wait for mount acknowledgements past the rebuilt round.
A rebuild first health-checks the current state and refuses a healthy state unless `FORCE` is supplied; a broken or absent state proceeds through the recovery path.

Rebuild edge reconstruction replays committed owner state and live precommit bindings, validates every committed `PartManifest` with `refMatchesBody` and `manifestNamespaceMatches`, and refuses the whole rebuild on a missing or invalid committed manifest body.

Rebuild edge accumulation is bounded by a memory budget: per-GC-shard edges are sorted and spilled into temporary run segments, then merged into one run using the T2 streaming readers and `RunFileWriter`.

The rebuild mints `new_round = max(observed_gc_round over all mount bodies, fence_round over all shards, and surviving gc/gen prefix numbers) + 1` so stale acknowledgements cannot float fresh condemnations past the floor.

A successful rebuild publishes an empty `retired_refs` set, preserving the reconstructed snapshot and making all content pass through the normal condemn → acknowledgement floor → graduate → delete pipeline again.

The rebuild command surface is `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD [FORCE] <disk>` and is logged through `CasGcScheduler` in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` with `gc_rebuild` audit events in `system.content_addressed_log`.

`clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild --disk <name> [--force]` opens the disk read-only without claiming the server-root mount or creating a heartbeat, takes the independent GC lease, and exits nonzero on refusal.
Rebuild refusal conditions are any missing or invalid committed manifest body, undecodable ref shard, unreadable mount body, healthy current state without `FORCE`, or failure to acquire the GC lease.

The rebuild implementation reuses `discoverUniverse`, `foldManifestEdges`, `foldDeltasIntoGeneration`, `computeHeartbeatFloor`, and `prefixEligible` rather than adding a new scanner or merge machinery.

The rebuild's per-shard guard is stricter than a global empty-baseline check: it fires for any shard with no sealed cursor whose journal proves trimmed history, while a shard born after the baseline passes because its journal starts at `transition_version` 1.

For trimmed-but-live precommits whose create event was trimmed, the rebuild lists `cas/manifests/` and over-protects manifests that are not committed, not named by a live-precommit binding, and not provably build-dead by `prefixEligible`.
`HeartbeatFloor` gains `max_ack`, computed from every decoded mount body including fenced and terminated bodies, because the rebuild needs the maximum observed acknowledgement to mint a safe round.
Live GCS probes found that the S3-compatible surface silently ignores `If-None-Match` and `If-Match` on PUT and DELETE, so the CAS capability probe refuses that mode with exit 48.
GCS conditional semantics require a non-`x-amz` authentication dialect: GOOG4-HMAC or OAuth Bearer; `x-goog-*` headers cannot be mixed into sigv4 requests because GCS returns `ExcessHeaderValues`.
GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 over the GCS XML endpoint enforced the full 12/12 conditional probe battery, showing that the CAS incompatibility is a signing-dialect problem rather than an API-migration problem.
GCS returns the object incarnation token in every PUT and HEAD response as `x-goog-generation`, eliminating the need for a post-PUT HEAD.

GCS `CompleteMultipartUpload` silently ignores `x-goog-if-generation-match`, while `Compose` enforces it; conditional writes therefore must not use multipart finalize, with unconditional multipart to a temporary key followed by conditional `Compose` as the production-grade large-blob path.

GCS generation mismatches return HTTP 412 with the literal XML body code `PreconditionFailed`, so the existing ClickHouse detectors `finalizeConditionalWrite` and `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` require no change.
The GCS conditional dialect maps `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0` and `If-Match: "<digits>"` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: <digits>` at the HTTP boundary.
The GCS conditional dialect rewrites a response's `x-goog-generation` to a quoted `ETag`, allowing existing ETag token plumbing, `HeadResult.token`, and token-exact deletion to remain unchanged.

GCS generation-dialect mode is explicit: `http_client = gcp_oauth` enables the dialect for the existing OAuth client, and `http_client = gcs_hmac` selects `PocoHTTPClientGCSHMAC`; there is no endpoint auto-detection.
`signGOOG4` signs the final request with `host` and every `x-goog-*` header, sets `x-goog-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD` and `x-goog-date`, and uses the scope terminator `goog4_request`.
The GOOG4 key derivation is `HMAC("GOOG4"+secret, date) → "auto" → "storage" → "goog4_request"`, and the signer includes canonical query parameters such as multipart and list parameters.

`applyGcsConditionalDialectToRequest` drops AWS authentication artifacts including `Authorization`, `X-Amz-Date`, `x-amz-content-sha256`, and `x-amz-security-token`, then renames remaining `x-amz-*` headers to `x-goog-*`.
The GCS dialect throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` for an `If-None-Match` value other than `*` and for a non-numeric `If-Match` value, rather than silently changing conditional semantics.
The GCS dialect throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before sending a conditional `CompleteMultipartUpload`, identified as POST with an `uploadId` query parameter and no `partNumber`.
`S3ObjectStorage` reports `TokenType::Generation` when its client uses the GCS conditional dialect; otherwise CAS tokens remain `TokenType::ETag`.

A generation-dialect CAS conditional write uses a single-part upload with the new `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` cap, defaulting to 1 GiB; a conditional write larger than the cap throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and names the future Compose path and setting.

The new write settings for generation stores are `s3_force_single_part_upload` (default `false`) and `s3_single_part_upload_max_bytes_override` (default `0`, disabled); setting the former makes `WriteBufferFromS3` refuse multipart creation.
The CAS capability probe calls `Backend::checkStorePreconditions` before its operation battery; the default hook is a no-op.
A generation-dialect GCS bucket with object versioning enabled is rejected with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because token-exact DELETE archives a noncurrent generation instead of reclaiming storage.

`isBucketVersioningEnabled` returns `std::nullopt` when the bucket versioning status is unknown or not applicable; the CAS probe fails closed when a generation-dialect storage explicitly reports versioning enabled.
Without `http_client = gcs_hmac`, existing disks retain byte-identical wire behavior; GCS generation binding is explicit opt-in only.
`PocoHTTPClientGCSHMAC` applies the GCS conditional dialect before GOOG4 signing, while `PocoHTTPClientGCPOAuth` applies the dialect before injecting the Bearer authorization header.
`http_client = gcs_hmac` forces `ApiMode::GCS` even when credentials are present, because the SDK-side GCS accommodations must remain active for GOOG4 requests.
`conditionalOpsUseGenerationTokens()` is a virtual object-storage capability that defaults to `false`; `S3ObjectStorage` returns whether its client uses the GCS conditional dialect.

GCS generation binding intentionally does not auto-detect the endpoint, implement Compose-based conditional finalize for blobs above the single-PUT cap, add JSON or resumable uploads, or add requester-pays `x-goog-user-project` support.

The live GCS acceptance cycle requires the capability probe to pass 8/8 plus versioning checks, then replication and checksums, churn with `OPTIMIZE FINAL`, two-phase reclaim observed in the bucket, clean fsck, and `DROP TABLE` to metadata-only.
OAuth validation with ADC credentials is optional for the release gate; failure is documented as HMAC-only support for now and does not block the GCS HMAC gate.
The exact CA disk setting controlling the generation-store conditional single-PUT budget is `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes`, with default `1ULL << 30`.
The GCS conditional-write path must never allow `CompleteMultipartUpload`; `WriteBufferFromS3` throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` before starting multipart when `s3_force_single_part_upload` is set.
A GCS versioned bucket is rejected even though per-operation conditional checks may pass, because versioning turns token-exact deletion into archival and silently prevents storage reclamation.

The GCS live validation fsck command is `clickhouse disks -C /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml --disk ca_ro --query 'fsck'`, and the acceptance result is `dangling=0 unreachable=0 unaccounted=0`, `dedup_ratio=2`.

The snapshot-streaming implementation requires `RunFileReader` to have no whole-run member, keeps `cur_block.size() <= kRunHardCapBlockSize`, and bounds every ranged request by `kRunHardCapBlockSize + 64 * 1024` plus the footer allowance.
The intended streaming open profile is exactly one HEAD, one tail ranged GET, and one body `getStream`; `seek` adds one ranged GET per touched block.

`RunFileReader(Backend &, const String & key)` treats an absent run, truncated stream, or CRC failure as `CORRUPTED_DATA`; the borrowed constructor is a zero-copy `std::string_view` over caller-owned bytes.
A pure reference-carry path requires both an empty delta bucket and an empty retired-merge input; an empty delta with prior retired entries still runs the merge so retired entries settle every pass.

In the mount-recovery plan, `claimMountAwaitingExpiry` exposes an optional `on_wait_start` callback that fires once with the observed lease and latched deadline so `Store::open` can emit an operator-visible log.
The mount-recovery plan requires a zero poll interval to be raised to a one-millisecond floor so the bounded wait cannot spin indefinitely.

The raw rebuild API returns `RebuildReport` with `performed`, `refusal`, minted `round` and `generation`, counts for namespaces, shards, committed refs, live precommits, unowned-alive manifests, edges, and clamped shards.

The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration over batches of at most `rebuild_edge_budget` edges, feeding the previous attempt's runs back as `prior_runs`; this provides O(budget) memory without new spill/merge classes.
The planned SQL rebuild surface converts `performed == false` into `BAD_ARGUMENTS` with the refusal text, while also recording the refusal in the GC log.
The `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` tool must use a read-only open, print rebuild counters one per line, print `refusal=<text>` on refusal, and never claim a live server's mount.

The generation-binding implementation's `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` cap buffers conditional single-PUT bodies in RAM; larger conditional writes fail rather than silently taking the multipart path.
The generation-binding implementation leaves the 412 `PreconditionFailed` detection code untouched because GCS and AWS expose the same body code.
The generation-binding plan does not modify `contrib/aws`; all GCS behavior is implemented in ClickHouse's HTTP, object-storage, and CAS layers.
The ack-floor redesign leaves read-path 404-repair B85 unchanged; it is explicitly outside this design's scope.
The mount-recovery plan restores real hard `docker kill -s KILL` for ClickHouse replicas while retaining RustFS's B145 graceful-only fault scope.
